scenario.name: test_failures_after_refactoring
scenario.description: When tests fail after refactoring changes

symptoms.symptom: Unit tests that were passing before refactoring now fail
Integration tests break due to changed interfaces

recovery_strategy.step: Rollback the refactoring changes
Fix the failing tests to work with new code structure
Re-run test suite to verify fixes
Investigate root cause of test failures
Profile performance before and after refactoring
Identify performance bottlenecks in refactored code
Revert problematic refactoring changes
Apply performance optimizations while maintaining code quality
Monitor performance metrics continuously

scenario.name: breaking_changes_detected
scenario.description: When refactoring unintentionally changes external behavior

symptoms.symptom: Client applications break due to interface changes

recovery_strategy.step: Immediately identify the scope of behavioral changes
Assess impact on external systems and clients
Create compatibility layer or adapter if needed
Document breaking changes and migration path
Coordinate with other teams for smooth transition
Consider rollback strategy if changes cannot be deployed

scenario.name: complexity_increases
scenario.description: When refactoring inadvertently makes code more complex

symptoms.symptom: Code becomes harder to understand and maintain
New developers struggle with the codebase

recovery_strategy.step: Analyze which refactoring changes increased complexity
Consider alternative approaches that achieve same goals with less complexity
Partially or fully revert complex refactoring
Add documentation explaining the complexity
Provide training on the new code structure

tactics.tactic: Write characterization tests before any refactoring
Run full test suite after each refactoring change
Use integration tests to catch interface changes
Perform regression testing on critical paths
Maintain high test coverage throughout refactoring process
Use property-based testing for complex objects

strategy.name: incremental_refactoring
strategy.description: Minimize risk through small, testable changes

tactics.tactic: Break large refactoring into multiple small steps
Test each increment before proceeding to next
Use feature flags to enable/disable new code paths
Maintain rollback capability at each step

strategy.name: behavior_preservation
strategy.description: Ensure refactoring doesn't change external behavior

tactics.tactic: Write comprehensive characterization tests for existing behavior
Use contract testing to verify interface compliance
Compare before/after behavior using golden master testing
Use property-based testing for state changes
Verify all edge cases are handled identically
Monitor behavior in staging environment before production deployment

procedure.name: git_rollback
procedure.description: Using version control to revert problematic changes

steps.step: Identify the commit that introduced the issue
Create a new branch from the stable commit
Test the reverted code to ensure it works correctly
Merge the fix back to main branch if needed

procedure.name: feature_flag_rollback
procedure.description: Using feature flags to disable problematic refactoring

steps.step: Implement feature flag to control new code path
Set flag to false to disable new behavior
Test that old behavior is restored
Document the flag and rollback procedure
